summary: Binary prediction of whether a protein binds a given small-molecule ligand, from the sequence and ligand SMILES.
what_it_measures: A 0/1 label for whether an enzyme–ligand pair is a binder. Positives come from BioLiP's biologically relevant ligand–protein interactions; negatives are generated by pairing proteins with ligands they are not annotated to bind.
assay_method: Structure-derived binding annotations from BioLiP (ligands observed in contact with protein residues in experimental structures), filtered to enzymes and to drug-like ligands.
provenance: Cleaned from the BioLiP non-redundant release: enzymes only (non-null EC), ligand IDs mapped to SMILES via the PDB Chemical Component Dictionary, monoatomic ions and polymers removed, then one negative sampled per positive (seed 42, deduplicated on sequence+SMILES).
when_to_use: A protein+ligand classification task probing recognition/binding; useful for virtual screening and substrate-scope questions.
caveats: Negatives are synthetic (a protein paired with a ligand it is not annotated to bind may still bind weakly), and BioLiP's structural coverage biases the positives. The ligand descriptors carry much of the signal, so absolute scores overstate what the protein representation adds; the comparison between PLMs is still fair because all receive the same descriptors.
